messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable football game with realistic gameplay, full teams and rosters, and graphics for all devices.

## Requirements
- User requested: “A 3d football 🏈 game that is the best out there with realistic real gameplay for gridiron masterpiece that pays it should be full rosters and full list of teams with all-real graphics for all devices”.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone browser game with canvas-rendered football gameplay, all 32 NFL team names, and responsive desktop/mobile layouts.
- Used fictional player names and ratings; this is an arcade-style 2D canvas game, not a fully realistic 3D game or licensed-real-graphics experience.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with a game menu, team matchup selection, a simulated field, player movement, passing, tackling, scoring, quarters, and win/lose flow.
- Added desktop keyboard controls and mobile touch controls.
- Added all 32 NFL team names and a fictional 11-player starting roster.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened the app in Playwright and inspected screenshots at `screenshots/menu.jpg` and `screenshots/game.jpg`.

### Active
- Finish and verify mobile team selection and game control updates made after the screenshot checks.
- Review final changes and summarize the implementation and its limitations for the user.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reopen or reload `http://localhost:3002` and verify desktop and mobile layouts, including mobile team selection and touch controls.
2. Check for gameplay or console errors; the earlier only observed console error was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
3. Report honestly that this is a playable arcade-style prototype, not a realistic 3D licensed football game.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, styling, team/roster data, and gameplay logic.
- `screenshots/menu.jpg`: Earlier menu screenshot.
- `screenshots/game.jpg`: Earlier gameplay screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Recent edits added mobile team selectors (`#homeMobile`, `#awayMobile`) synchronized with desktop selectors and made mobile controls responsive to viewport width; these edits have not yet been reverified.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e09164ba5ffetTH4K63hIEazqF" state="completed">
## Findings — `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`

### Initialization and controls

- **Team-selection setup throws on startup.** In `initSelect()` at **line 20**, the code queries `#homeMobile` and `#awayMobile`, but those elements are absent from the markup at **lines 12–13**. The first attempt to append an option to the missing mobile select throws, so initialization stops: the desktop selectors are only partly populated, and their change handlers and roster rendering never run.
- **The start buttons are still wired.** Their handlers are assigned *before* `initSelect()` is called on **line 104**. So this error does not prevent the click handlers from being registered; instead, starting the game can use the incomplete selectors and wrong team values. The smallest fix is to remove mobile-select references if mobile team selectors aren’t intended, or add those elements and guard against missing selectors before using them.
- **Forward movement is up/W.** Movement is read at **line 93**: up/W decreases `y`, which advances the carrier toward the touchdown condition at **line 100**. Down/S moves backward. This matches the on-screen hint at **line 12**, but may feel unintuitive if players expect “upfield” to mean another direction.
- **Input can become stuck.** Key state is set on `keydown` and cleared on `keyup` at **lines 102–103**. If the window loses focus before a keyup arrives, the key can remain active. Clear held keys on window blur or document visibility changes. A focus guard for form controls would also prevent gameplay keys from firing while a selector is focused.
- **The reported yardage is disconnected from the displayed ball spot.** On tackles, **line 84** calculates gain from a fixed starting `y` value, then updates `spot`; meanwhile, **line 69** resets the carrier to `y=76` for each formation. This means the displayed spot and actual field position aren’t driving each other. Track the play’s starting position and calculate the result from that, then use the updated spot when placing the next formation.
- **Incomplete passes do not gain yards.** **Line 85** advances the down while leaving `toGo` unchanged. That is appropriate for a no-gain incomplete pass; the `toGo=toGo` assignment is just redundant. It is not, by itself, the advance blocker.

### UI room

The game already has a scoreboard, drive pill, callout, toast, and bottom hint in the overlay (**line 12**); their layout is in the compact stylesheet on **line 7**. The desktop layout also has a side panel, while the panel is hidden on narrow screens.

- **Play-by-play:** Use the desktop side panel for a compact event log during play, rather than adding another persistent overlay over the field.
- **Replay and rewards:** A replay control could sit near the drive/status area; show achievements or rewards in an end-of-game summary or brief callout/toast.
- **Mobile:** Keep additions away from the bottom edge, where the touch controls, hint, and toast compete for space. Prefer a brief, dismissible event card in an open area above the controls.

No files were modified.
</subagent>

### Browser testing

- This is a standalone HTML game at `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`; it has no package manifest or project-specific Playwright test suite.

- `endPlay` handles touchdowns, tackles, incomplete passes, and interceptions. Pass outcomes include randomness, so passing assertions may be nondeterministic.
- `updateHUD` updates score, clock, and down/distance. `frame` drives the animation loop.

## Objective
- Turn the existing browser football prototype into a playable, more engaging game with reliable ball progression.
- Add instant replay, play-by-play, and achievement rewards with a career pay scale.

## Requirements
- Aim for Madden-like gameplay and presentation, while making reasonable assumptions without asking follow-up questions.
- Support desktop and mobile controls and graphics; use fictional rosters and avoid implying licensed player names or graphics.

## Decisions
- Keep the project as a standalone browser canvas prototype rather than attempting a licensed simulation.
- Use locally saved, one-time career rewards for achievements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed team selection initialization and kept the existing mobile team selectors synchronized.
- Added play-by-play, career pay/achievement, and replay UI styling.
- Implemented snap-on-movement/pass, field-position-based formations and yardage, downs, turnover handling, passing completion, and opponent drive simulation.
- Added replay frame capture/playback and persistent rewards for first down, first completion, explosive play, and first touchdown.

### Active
- Validate JavaScript and run an interactive desktop/mobile playthrough; inspect console errors and confirm movement, passing, HUD updates, rewards, and replay.
- Refine any issues found during testing.

### Blocked
- Browser testing has not yet been run; a new local server attempt on port 3000 failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`. An existing server may already be available.

## Next Move
1. Run a syntax check on the script in `index.html`.
2. Open the existing local server in Playwright and verify menu initialization, movement, passing, down/distance, commentary, rewards, and replay.
3. Test a narrow viewport and touch controls; fix any issues discovered.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: standalone game markup, styles, team/roster data, and all gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Changes to `index.html` are uncommitted.
- No project-specific browser test suite was found; `playwright-cli` is available.
- The prototype still simulates the opponent’s drive and uses simplified football rules; it is not a full licensed simulation.

## Objective
- Make the existing browser football prototype playable and more engaging, with reliable ball progression.
- Add instant replay, play-by-play, and achievement rewards with career pay.

## Requirements
- Aim for Madden-like gameplay and presentation, making reasonable assumptions without follow-up questions.
- Support desktop and mobile controls and graphics; use fictional rosters and avoid implying licensed player names or graphics.

## Decisions
- Keep the project as a standalone browser canvas prototype rather than attempting a licensed simulation.
- Save one-time career achievement rewards locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed team selection initialization and synchronized desktop/mobile team selectors.
- Added play-by-play, career pay/achievement, and replay UI styling.
- Implemented movement/pass snapping, field-position-based formations and yardage, downs, turnover handling, passing, and simulated opponent drives.
- Added replay capture/playback and locally persisted rewards for first down, first completion, explosive play, and first touchdown.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check`.
- Browser-tested menu, movement, down/distance updates, interception commentary, and instant replay.
- Fixed mobile-control visibility on resize, replay availability during live plays, post-play status, and mobile overlay placement.

### Active
- Continue desktop/mobile playthrough testing, especially touch controls, pass completions, achievement rewards, replay behavior, and mobile layout after the latest styling changes.
- Review remaining gameplay edge cases and confirm the fictional presentation meets the roster/licensing constraint.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, including team selection, touch controls, rewards, and mobile layout.
2. Check browser console; the only observed error was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
3. Fix any issues found and rerun the syntax check.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: standalone game markup, styles, team/roster data, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. The current repository status also showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Browser smoke test showed a 4-yard run updating the drive to `2ND & 6 · BALL ON 29`; passing produced an interception in that test, and replay entered `INSTANT REPLAY · SLOW MOTION`.
- The first narrow-screen screenshot was captured before the latest overlay repositioning; mobile visual confirmation is still pending.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Make the browser football prototype playable and engaging, with reliable ball progression, instant replay, play-by-play, and achievement rewards.

## Requirements
- Aim for Madden-like gameplay and presentation, making reasonable assumptions without follow-up questions.
- Support desktop and mobile controls and graphics.
- Use fictional rosters and avoid implying licensed player names or graphics.

## Decisions
- Keep the project as a standalone browser canvas prototype rather than attempting a licensed simulation.
- Save one-time career achievement rewards locally.
- Replace real-world league team identities with original fictional teams to meet the fictional-presentation requirement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed team selection initialization and synchronized desktop/mobile team selectors.
- Implemented movement/pass snapping, formations, downs, turnovers, passing, simulated opponent drives, replay, and local achievement rewards.
- Added play-by-play, career pay, replay UI, and mobile-control visibility/layout adjustments.
- Replaced the real-world team list with 32 fictional teams and updated scoreboard defaults and menu copy.
- Verified `index.html` script syntax with `node --check`.
- Browser-tested desktop menu, movement, down/distance updates, interception commentary, replay, and team-selection options.

### Active
- Continue desktop/mobile playthrough testing, especially touch controls, pass completions, achievement rewards, replay behavior, and mobile layout.
- Review gameplay edge cases and confirm fictional presentation throughout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, including team selection, touch controls, rewards, replay, and mobile layout.
2. Check for any browser console errors; the earlier only observed error was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
3. Fix issues found and rerun the JavaScript syntax check.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: standalone game markup, styles, fictional teams/roster data, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Repository status showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Desktop smoke test showed a 4-yard run updating the drive to `2ND & 6 · BALL ON 29`; passing produced an interception in that test, and replay entered `INSTANT REPLAY · SLOW MOTION`.
- The most recent mobile test confirmed fictional team options and defaults (`Northstar Navigators` vs `Ashford Arrows`), but mobile gameplay and layout still need visual verification.

## Objective
- Make the standalone browser football prototype playable and engaging, with reliable ball progression, replay, play-by-play, and achievement rewards.

## Requirements
- Aim for Madden-like gameplay and presentation, with desktop and mobile controls and graphics.
- Use fictional rosters and avoid implying licensed player names or graphics.

## Decisions
- Keep the project as a standalone browser canvas prototype.
- Save one-time career achievement rewards locally.
- Use original fictional teams and players rather than real-world league identities.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented team selection, movement and passing, formations, downs, turnovers, simulated opponent drives, replay, play-by-play, and local achievement rewards.
- Replaced team identities with 32 fictional teams; updated default scoreboard identities and menu copy.
- Tested the mobile layout at 390×844, confirmed fictional team options, started a game, and verified touch controls are displayed.
- Tested mobile directional input: play snapped and advanced the ball four yards to `2ND & 6 · BALL ON 29`.
- Tested mobile pass input; pass-in-air commentary appeared.
- Verified extracted game script with `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`; browser console reported zero errors.

### Active
- Continue testing pass completion, rewards, replay behavior, and mobile layout/gameplay.
- Review gameplay edge cases and confirm fictional presentation throughout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, especially pass completion, achievement rewards, replay, and touch controls.
2. Check mobile layout during active gameplay and watch for browser console errors.
3. Fix issues found and rerun the JavaScript syntax check.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: standalone game markup, styles, fictional teams and roster, and gameplay logic.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Recent mobile test showed `NSN` Northstar Navigators vs `ASA` Ashford Arrows; directional input updated down and distance correctly.
- Pass test reached “Pass in the air to a receiver”; completion and reward persistence remain unverified.

- Make the standalone browser football prototype playable and engaging, with reliable ball progression, replay, play-by-play, and achievement rewards.

## Requirements
- Aim for Madden-like gameplay and presentation, with desktop and mobile controls and graphics.

- Save one-time career achievement rewards locally.
